explication:
Apache JMeter is a multi-module Gradle monorepo for load testing. Its architecture is centered on a shared test-plan model, an execution engine, pluggable protocol samplers, and multiple result-processing paths for GUI, CLI, and reporting.

1. Core execution model  
`src/core` contains the fundamental runtime: `TestElement`, `HashTree`-based test plans, thread groups, samplers, listeners, timers, assertions, config elements, and the `StandardJMeterEngine`. This is the main execution backbone used by both GUI and non-GUI runs.

2. Test plan lifecycle  
A typical flow is: author or import a test plan, serialize it to JMX/XML, load it back into the tree model, precompile it, then execute it through `JMeterThread` instances. The engine resolves functions, variables, config merging, and scoped elements before sampling starts.

3. GUI subsystem  
The Swing-based IDE lives mostly in `src/core` and `src/components`, with `MainFrame`, tree models, menus, actions, and many component-specific GUIs. It is not just a view layer: it is the primary editor for composing the test tree, controlling runs, viewing results, and launching report generation.

4. Protocol-specific samplers as plug-in modules  
Protocol support is split into dedicated modules under `src/protocol/*`: HTTP, JDBC, JMS, FTP, LDAP, TCP, Java, JUnit, mail/SMTP, native/system, and Bolt. Each module contributes samplers, config elements, GUIs, parsers, and resources, and plugs into the same core `Sampler`/`ConfigElement`/`Visualizer` contracts.

5. HTTP stack as the largest protocol boundary  
`src/protocol/http` is the most elaborate subsystem. It includes HTTP samplers, request builders, cookies, cache, auth, proxy/recording, HTML/CSS link extraction, curl parsing, and mirror-server support. This module is a full HTTP client/recording/correlation stack rather than a thin sampler wrapper.

6. Result collection and listeners  
Samples flow from samplers into listeners and collectors in `src/core` and `src/components`. Important consumers include `ResultCollector`, `Summariser`, visualizers, and backend listeners. They can persist raw results, compute summaries, render live graphs, or forward metrics to external systems.

7. Reporting pipeline  
The HTML dashboard/reporting system is in `src/core/src/main/java/org/apache/jmeter/report/**`. It reads sample logs, converts them into report data, runs aggregations and graph consumers, and emits static HTML/JSON dashboard artifacts. This is separate from the live GUI visualizers and is designed for post-run analysis.

8. Live metrics backends  
`src/components` contains backend listeners for Graphite and InfluxDB. These modules transform sample events into time-series metrics and send them over network protocols, enabling external observability tools to visualize test execution in near real time.

9. Save/load and serialization layer  
`src/core/src/main/java/org/apache/jmeter/save` handles JMX/XML persistence, CSV result I/O, and XStream-based converters. This layer is the boundary between in-memory test trees/results and disk artifacts such as test plans, result logs, and report inputs.

10. Remote/distributed execution  
The engine supports remote test execution through RMI-related classes in `src/core/src/main/java/org/apache/jmeter/engine` and `src/core/src/main/java/org/apache/jmeter/rmi`. The client/remote engine split allows a controller node to launch and coordinate test threads on remote agents.

11. Functions, scripting, and extensibility  
`src/functions`, `src/components`, and `src/protocol/java` provide a large function library and scriptable samplers/processors. JSR223, BeanShell, Groovy, regex/XPath/JSON extractors, and test bean infrastructure make the system extensible without changing the core engine.

12. Shared utility foundation  
`src/jorphan` is the shared support library used across modules. It provides collections, GUI helpers, reflection/service loading, logging wrappers, math/statistics, I/O utilities, and legacy compatibility classes. Many higher-level modules depend on it for non-domain-specific behavior.

13. Launchers, packaging, and distribution  
`src/launcher` contains startup entry points, while `src/dist` and `src/dist-check` verify assembled distributions. The top-level `bin` and `lib` directories define the runtime layout, scripts, examples, templates, and bundled resources used when JMeter is shipped or run from a distribution.

14. Build and test architecture  
The repository is built with Gradle and uses many module-level test suites, fixtures, and benchmark sources (`jmh`). Mixed Java/Kotlin code appears in core domains such as schemas, DSL/tree building, open-model thread groups, and GUI bindings, indicating a gradual modernization layer over the older Java/Swing architecture.

Overall data flow: test plan authoring or import → model tree persistence → engine precompilation → threaded sampling against protocol modules → listeners/reporters/backends → saved results and optional dashboard generation.
